outcome: No proof or disproof of the Grothendieck-Katz p-curvature conjecture has appeared since 26 January 2024; the in-window events are partial results (a non-abelian Katz theorem for isomonodromy foliations by Lam and Litt, privileged local systems in every dimension by Esnault and Groechenig, an effective bound for order-one equations, an equivalence with the ESBT Conjecture F, and a generalized algebraic-integrability verification for separable vector fields), one withdrawn preprint whose author now doubts the conjecture, and several discarded items.
problem_asks: (1) Let S be a smooth scheme over a finitely generated subring R of C and (E, nabla) a flat (integrable) connection on S. The statement asks for an equivalence of two conditions: (i) some finite etale cover S' of S_C trivialises (E, nabla), equivalently the monodromy of (E, nabla) over C is finite, equivalently the complex system has a full set of algebraic solutions; (ii) the p-curvature of the reduction of (E, nabla) modulo p vanishes for almost all primes p. (2) The direction (ii) implies (i): vanishing p-curvature for almost all p forces finite monodromy and a full set of algebraic solutions over C (the 'local-global' direction, which Grothendieck is said to have conjectured to be sufficient). (3) The direction (i) implies (ii): finite monodromy forces vanishing p-curvature for almost all p (the necessary-condition direction). (4) Scope: as stated for flat connections of any rank on any smooth S over R. The Wikipedia bullet's wording is 'a conjectured local-global principle for linear ordinary differential equations', i.e. the rank-n linear ODE case; the current Wikipedia article reduces the essential case to rational functions with rational coefficients (that article revision is not the frozen one, so this is recorded as context only). Both readings are recorded; the later pass decides which the bullet asks.

events.what_happened: Nicholas Katz, 'Algebraic solutions of differential equations (p-curvature and the Hodge filtration)', Inventiones Mathematicae 18 (1972), 1-118, DOI 10.1007/BF01389714. The paper publishes the conjecture (attributed to Grothendieck, who discussed it publicly in 1969 without writing it down) and proves it for Gauss-Manin connections on the cohomology of smooth projective families and for Picard-Fuchs equations. The Princeton PDF of the article is an image scan with no text layer, so the statements here are taken from Lam-Litt (arXiv 2601.07933, Theorem 1.1.1) and secondary descriptions, not from Katz's text.
events.delivers: Restricted case: the conjecture for Gauss-Manin connections on H^i of smooth projective families. As Lam-Litt state it, if the p-curvature vanishes mod p for infinitely many p then the monodromy on H^i(X_s(C), Z) factors through a finite group (note: 'infinitely many' primes, a weaker hypothesis than 'almost all'). Also covers Picard-Fuchs equations.
events.remains: Flat connections over arbitrary smooth S that are not Gauss-Manin; the general statement for all ranks.
events.direction: Proves the finite-monodromy side for the Gauss-Manin class, i.e. the conjecture holds there.

events.what_happened: Honda's proof of the p-curvature conjecture for first-order equations y' = u y with u rational (the arXiv paper 2510.00892 calls it an elementary proof and cites it as [Hon81]). It reduces the question to Kronecker's theorem: an irreducible rational polynomial with a root mod almost every p has a rational root. Talk abstracts by Pannier date Honda's result to 1974. The Chudnovsky brothers gave a second proof in 1985 via Pade approximation. The Honda original was not opened; this is relayed from search excerpts and from arXiv 2510.00892.
events.revisions: Date conflict: 1974 per talk abstracts; cited as [Hon81] in arXiv 2510.00892 (Honda's venue and year not verified). Chudnovsky second proof 1985.
events.delivers: Order-one equations with rational coefficients (Fürnsinn-Pannier say polynomial coefficients). For these the conjecture holds: vanishing p-curvature for almost all p gives a non-zero algebraic solution.
events.remains: All equations of order two or more.

checked_by.who: D. V. and G. V. Chudnovsky
checked_by.qualification: Authors of a second proof of Kronecker's theorem and Honda's theorem by Pade approximation
checked_by.what_they_did: Gave a second proof (1985) according to Fürnsinn-Pannier and search excerpts; not inspected

events.direction: Confirms the finite-monodromy side for order-one equations.
people: Honda (given name not in sources read)

events.what_happened: Katz, Rigid Local Systems (Annals of Mathematics Studies 139, 1996), Theorem 9.4.1, as cited by Esnault-Groechenig (arXiv 2606.16873, Section 3): rigid local systems with fixed quasi-unipotent monodromy on open subsets of P^1 satisfy the p-curvature conjecture; the proof uses middle convolution. The book was not opened; this is taken from Esnault-Groechenig.
events.delivers: Rigid local systems on curves (open subsets of P^1) with fixed quasi-unipotent monodromy.
events.remains: Non-rigid local systems; higher-dimensional varieties.
events.direction: Confirms the finite-monodromy side for rigid local systems on curves.

events.what_happened: Benson Farb and Mark Kisin, 'The Grothendieck-Katz Conjecture for certain locally symmetric varieties', arXiv:0807.1152 (8 July 2008, single version as listed). Uses Margulis's results on lattices in semisimple Lie groups to prove the conjecture for certain locally symmetric varieties, including the moduli space A_g of abelian varieties for g > 1.
events.revisions: v1 only as listed on the arXiv page read.
events.delivers: Restricted class: the conjecture for certain locally symmetric varieties (abstract names A_g, g > 1).
events.remains: All other varieties and the general statement.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for the listed class.

events.what_happened: Esnault and Langer, 'On a positive equicharacteristic variant of the p-curvature conjecture', arXiv:1108.0103 (first posted 30 July 2011; v3 April 2012; Documenta Math. 18 (2013)). Formulates and proves a weak form in equal characteristic p > 0, and states a counterexample to a strong form of it. Abstract read; statements not read.
events.delivers: A different question: an equal-characteristic analogue, not the characteristic-zero statement. The counterexample is to a strong form of that analogue (the abstract does not say which).
events.remains: The characteristic-zero conjecture as stated in the problem.
events.direction: Not about the problem as stated; a discarded analogue, recorded for completeness.
events.object: A counterexample to a strong form of the equal-characteristic p-curvature variant; its content was not read.

events.what_happened: Yunqing Tang, 'Algebraic solutions of differential equations over the projective line minus three points', arXiv:1412.7875 (v1 26 Dec 2014; v2 21 Sep 2015); Int. J. Number Theory 14(5), 2018. Proves a variant for P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}: if a convergence condition holds for all primes p, the monodromy is trivial; similar variants for an elliptic curve and P^1 minus {+-1, +-i, infinity}.
events.delivers: A variant on P^1 minus three points (and two other curves), under a convergence hypothesis holding for all p; the abstract says the convergence condition is implied by vanishing p-curvature where defined. Not the stated conjecture; the exact convergence condition was not read.
events.remains: The conjecture itself on P^1 minus three points without the convergence hypothesis, and all other varieties.
events.direction: A variant result; does not settle the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Ananth N. Shankar, 'The p-curvature conjecture and monodromy about simple closed loops', arXiv:1610.05674 (18 Oct 2016); Duke Math. J. 167(10) (2018), 1951-1980. Proves that if the variety is a generic curve, every simple closed loop on it has finite monodromy under the almost-all-primes vanishing hypothesis.
events.delivers: Restricted case: generic curves; the conclusion is finite monodromy on each simple closed loop (a local statement on the curve), not finite monodromy of the whole connection.
events.remains: Higher-dimensional varieties; the whole monodromy group on non-generic curves.
events.direction: Partial, restricted to generic curves; the abstract does not claim the full conjecture.

events.what_happened: Esnault and Groechenig, 'Rigid connections and F-isocrystals', arXiv:1707.00752 (first posted 3 July 2017; v4 1 June 2020 marked as accepted in Acta Mathematica 225 (2020), 103-158). The abstract states that irreducible rigid flat connections with vanishing p-curvature are unitary, which 'allows us to prove new cases of the Grothendieck-Katz p-curvature conjecture'.
events.revisions: v1 3 Jul 2017; v2 8 Feb 2018; v3 9 Jul 2018; v4 1 Jun 2020 (accepted in Acta Math).
events.delivers: Restricted class: irreducible rigid flat connections (vanishing p-curvature implies unitary, hence finite monodromy); the authors call the result 'new cases' of the conjecture.
events.remains: Non-rigid connections; the general statement.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper per the v4 comment; refereeing not inspected

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for a restricted class (irreducible rigid connections).

events.what_happened: Anand Patel, Ananth N. Shankar and Junho Peter Whang, arXiv:1811.04538 (v1 12 Nov 2018; v2 4 Feb 2019; v3 31 May 2019, titled 'The rank two p-curvature conjecture on generic curves'). The v3 abstract: the conjecture is proved for rank two vector bundles with connection on generic curves, by deformation techniques for families of varieties plus topological arguments. Search excerpts say the v1 title was 'The p-curvature conjecture in families' and that the paper also treats generic fibres of families; the v1 page was not opened. Journal reference (Adv. Math. 386 (2021)) is from a search summary, not verified.
events.revisions: v1 12 Nov 2018; v2 4 Feb 2019; v3 31 May 2019 (no version after January 2024).
events.delivers: Restricted case: rank two bundles with connection on generic curves. The v3 comments say the main result was improved to all generic curves.
events.remains: Rank three and higher; non-generic curves; higher dimension.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for rank two on generic curves.

events.what_happened: Max Menzies, 'The p-curvature conjecture for the non-abelian Gauss-Manin connection', Harvard PhD thesis, arXiv:1912.05757 (12 Dec 2019). Defines a non-abelian Gauss-Manin connection and its p-curvature on the stack of vector bundles with integrable connection, which requires a generalized form of the conjecture (Bost, Ekedahl, Shepherd-Barron); shows the analogue of the main technical step of Katz's theorem holds. The thesis states 'It is at present open, though various cases are known.'
events.delivers: A non-abelian analogue of a technical step in Katz's Gauss-Manin theorem. Not a proof of any case of the stated conjecture; it sets up the generalized conjecture.
events.remains: The conjecture itself and the generalized non-abelian conjecture.
events.direction: Analogue of a technical step; no case of the stated conjecture settled.

events.what_happened: Alin Bostan, Xavier Caruso and Julien Roques, 'Algebraic solutions of linear differential equations: an arithmetic approach', arXiv:2304.05061 (v1 11 Apr 2023; v2 22 Aug 2024; to appear in Bull. AMS). An expository paper that presents the local-global arithmetic approach 'initiated by Grothendieck in the late sixties' and states that it 'leads to the still unsolved Grothendieck-Katz p-curvature conjecture'. No new result about the conjecture is claimed in the abstract.
events.revisions: v1 11 Apr 2023; v2 22 Aug 2024 (revision inside the window, content change not inspected).
events.delivers: Nothing new about the conjecture: exposition and an explicit status statement that it is unsolved.
events.remains: All parts of problem_asks.
events.direction: Expository; neither supports nor cuts against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Hossein Movasati (IMPA), 'Grothendieck-Katz conjecture', arXiv:2403.11829 (v1 Mon 18 Mar 2024; v2 9 May 2024; v3 25 Feb 2025, withdrawn). The v1 abstract, as read on the arXiv abstract page: linear differential equations whose solutions are all algebraic have zero m-curvature mod p^k for all but finitely many primes p, for all k and m with ord_p(m!) >= k. The author calls this a reformulation of the Grothendieck-Katz conjecture under a stronger hypothesis. The withdrawal notice says the article 'is now a section of a new article Leaf scheme and Hodge loci' (arXiv 2502.19988). The PDF is not readable through the fetch tool and the ar5iv page is empty, so the body and its theorems were not read.
events.revisions: v1 18 Mar 2024; v2 9 May 2024; v3 25 Feb 2025 (withdrawn; abstract now points to 2502.19988).
events.delivers: Per the abstract only: the implication 'algebraic solutions => vanishing m-curvature mod p^k for almost all p' (higher m, higher powers of p), which runs in the direction opposite to the conjecture's 'vanishing => algebraic'. The author presents the stated conjecture-direction as a reformulation with a stronger hypothesis.
events.remains: The conjecture's direction (vanishing p-curvature for almost all p implies algebraic solutions) is not established; the converse, which the author calls Conjecture 1.1 in the successor paper, is posed as open.
events.doubts: The author's own successor paper (arXiv 2502.19988, Section 1 and Section 1.6) says 'the content of Chapter 1 leads us to believe that the Grothendieck-Katz conjecture might be false' and that a consequence of it (Conjecture 1.3) 'might be false'. The doubt rests on a Lamé equation example (Proposition 1.2 in the successor) where the p-curvature vanishes for p = 5 while a higher-order iterate does not vanish mod 5^6. The author states 'the author is not aware of a counterexample' (Section 1.8 of the successor). No counterexample to the conjecture as stated is claimed.

withdrawn.what: Preprint v3 (25 Feb 2025) withdrawn; the arXiv abstract says the article is now a section of 'Leaf scheme and Hodge loci' (arXiv 2502.19988).

events.direction: Proves a higher-m, higher-power vanishing consequence of algebraicity (opposite implication to the conjecture). Its own paper says it is a reformulation under a stronger hypothesis, and the withdrawal makes the status of its claims unclear.

events.what_happened: Yeuk Hay Joshua Lam and Daniel Litt, 'Algebraicity and integrality of solutions to differential equations', arXiv:2501.13175 (submitted 22 Jan 2025; single version listed). Proposes a conjecture characterising algebraic solutions of possibly non-linear algebraic ODEs by the primes in the denominators of Taylor coefficients at a non-singular point. Section 1 says 'for linear equations, [it] is apparently strictly stronger than the pp-curvature conjecture' (Remark 1.1.4 says 'a priori much stronger'). They prove their conjecture in linear cases: Picard-Fuchs equations at cycle-class initial conditions (Theorem 1.3.3), Picard-Fuchs equations of families of elliptic curves with no initial-condition assumption (Theorem 1.3.4), and a local singular-point prediction for hypergeometric functions (Proposition 5.2.2). In the non-linear case: isomonodromy equations such as Painleve VI and Schlesinger systems at Picard-Fuchs initial conditions.
events.revisions: v1 only as listed on the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Verifies the STRONGER conjecture (their own) for the listed linear equations, which include Picard-Fuchs families; Section 1 quotes 'proving our conjecture for only certain isomonodromy ODE (and all initial conditions) would suffice to prove the classical Grothendieck-Katz pp-curvature conjecture in full generality.' The classical conjecture is not proved here; the Picard-Fuchs cases are already covered by Katz (1972).
events.remains: The classical conjecture in full; their conjecture in full; the nonlinear conjecture for general initial conditions.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for the verified classes; no counterexample; the authors' stronger statement is not the classical statement.

events.what_happened: Hossein Movasati, 'Leaf schemes and Hodge loci', arXiv:2502.19988 (v1 submitted 27 Feb 2025; v2 14 Dec 2025, current). A collection of sections on arithmetic properties of differential equations, foliations and Hodge loci; the successor to the withdrawn 2403.11829. Section 1 raises doubts about the Grothendieck-Katz conjecture and states its converse as Conjecture 1.1; Section 2 analyses Lame equations. The arXiv v1 header date reads 'February 25, 2025' while the submission date reads 27 February 2025; the arXiv date is used here.
events.revisions: v1 27 Feb 2025 (page header 25 Feb 2025); v2 14 Dec 2025 (current).
events.delivers: No proof of the conjecture. It restates the m-curvature theorem from 2403.11829 in a wider framework, proposes a local-global conjecture for leaf schemes, and raises the converse of the conjecture as Conjecture 1.1 with a Lame-equation example (Proposition 1.2).
events.remains: The whole conjecture: nothing here settles any direction.
events.doubts: Section 1 says 'the content of Chapter 1 leads us to believe that the Grothendieck-Katz conjecture might be false', and Section 1.6 says the author's impression is that a consequence of it 'might be false'. The basis is a Lame equation (Proposition 1.2) where the p-curvature vanishes at p = 5 but a higher iterate does not vanish mod 5^6; the author says 'the author is not aware of a counterexample' (Section 1.8). The author describes Section 2 as 'purely computational and experimental'. Only the first ~100,000 characters of the HTML were read.
events.direction: Raises doubt about the conjecture (or a consequence of it) without claiming a counterexample; restates the m-curvature result as a theorem.
events.object: A Lame equation (Proposition 1.2 in the successor) whose p-curvature vanishes at p = 5 while a higher-order iterate does not vanish mod 5^6; offered as evidence against the converse-type consequence, not as a counterexample to the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Yujie Xu, 'p-integrability', arXiv:2507.22056 (submitted 29 July 2025; single version). Proves that the Grothendieck-Katz p-curvature conjecture is equivalent to Conjecture F of Ekedahl, Shepherd-Barron and Taylor (ESBT99, an unpublished 1999 preprint). The equivalence is in both directions: Conjecture F implies the p-curvature conjecture, and the p-curvature conjecture implies Conjecture F for the foliation attached to a vector bundle with integrable connection. The PDF's own header says the notes were 'last polished in September 2021' and written as a first-year Harvard graduate student; the arXiv posting is 2025.
events.revisions: v1 29 Jul 2025 only. Notes internally dated September 2021 (polish date).
events.delivers: An equivalence between the conjecture and ESBT Conjecture F, a statement about algebraic integrability of foliations. It does not establish the truth of either. Remark 15 records that Bost proved conditional versions of both.
events.remains: Both the conjecture and Conjecture F, in full.
events.direction: Equivalence, neither way on truth: relates the conjecture to a stronger foliation statement.

events.what_happened: Florian Fürnsinn and Lucas Pannier, 'An Effective Version of the p-Curvature Conjecture for Order One Differential Equations', arXiv:2510.00892 (v1 1 Oct 2025; v2 12 Mar 2026, current). Combines Honda's proof for order-one equations with polynomial coefficients with an effective Kronecker theorem (Chudnovsky-style Hermite-Pade asymptotics) to bound the number of primes whose p-curvature must vanish before one concludes a non-zero algebraic solution exists, in terms of the height and degree of the coefficients. Describes an algorithm, implemented in SageMath (code on GitHub per the paper's Section 6.1).
events.delivers: Effective version of the conjecture for order-one equations with polynomial coefficients (Honda's theorem made effective: a bound on the number of primes). Theorem 1.2 (the bound) and Theorem 1.3 (complexity) are not stated in the parts read; the proof sketch gives sigma of order Delta_b^6 B up to logs.
events.remains: Order two and higher; the general statement.
events.directly_checkable: SageMath implementation of the algorithm, stated in the paper (Section 6.1) to be on GitHub with examples; not opened.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for order-one equations with an effective bound; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Yeuk Hay Joshua Lam and Daniel Litt, 'p-Curvature and Non-Abelian Cohomology', arXiv:2601.07933 (submitted 12 Jan 2026; single version; CC BY 4.0; 45 pages). Theorem A: if the p-curvature of the isomonodromy foliation on the moduli of rank r flat bundles on X/S vanishes mod p for infinitely many p, the action of pi_1(S, s) on the rank r integral characters of pi_1(X_s) factors through a finite group. Theorem B adds the hypothesis that every irreducible component of the Betti moduli space has a Z-bar point, and concludes that the action on the complex points factors through a finite group, so all leaves are algebraic. They state the classical conjecture follows for Gauss-Manin connections as an immediate consequence of Theorem 1.1.1 (which is Katz's theorem). They also verify the Ekedahl-Shepherd-Barron-Taylor/Bost conjecture for the isomonodromy foliation when r = 2, when the Betti space is irreducible, or for a relative curve.
events.revisions: v1 12 Jan 2026 only (page read states the acknowledgement text 'to be added after the referee process is complete', so the posted version is pre-refereeing).
events.delivers: A non-abelian analogue for rank r flat bundles over a smooth projective family, with the weaker hypothesis 'infinitely many p' (not almost all). For the classical conjecture, they say the Gauss-Manin case follows, which Katz already proved (1972). Their 'stacky' conjecture is said to hold for the moduli stack of de Rham bundles under mild hypotheses. The classical conjecture for arbitrary flat bundles is not addressed.
events.remains: The classical conjecture for arbitrary flat bundles (not Gauss-Manin or rank-r moduli of isomonodromy type); the full ESBT/Bost conjecture; Theorem B's arithmetic hypothesis in general.
events.direction: Extends Katz's Gauss-Manin theorem to a non-abelian setting; supports the conjecture's finite-monodromy direction in that setting. The stated classical consequence for Gauss-Manin is Katz's old result.

events.what_happened: Michael Barz, 'Non-Abelian p-Curvature and a Non-Abelian Katz's Formula', arXiv:2604.20054 (21 Apr 2026, single version). Gives a conceptual proof, using sheared de Rham stacks (Bhatt, Kanaev, Vologodsky, Zhang; Drinfeld), of a non-abelian Katz formula relating the Kodaira-Spencer map to the p-curvature of the Gauss-Manin connection; carries out a suggestion of Lam and Litt; the author says the result 'differs slightly' from theirs. Abstract read only.
events.delivers: A re-derivation of a formula underlying Lam-Litt's non-abelian Katz theorem; not a new case of the conjecture.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.

checked_by.qualification: Author of the write-up; qualifications not established from the sources read
checked_by.what_they_did: Gave an alternative proof of a formula used in Lam-Litt, noting a slight difference from their statement

events.direction: Neutral; supports the technique behind Lam-Litt. No new case of the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Hélène Esnault and Michael Groechenig, 'The Grothendieck-Katz Conjecture for privileged local systems', arXiv:2606.16873 (submitted 15 Jun 2026; single version; 15 pages). Defines privileged local systems on a smooth quasi-projective complex variety with fixed quasi-unipotent monodromy along a boundary divisor (a notion generalising Katz's physical rigidity to any dimension). Theorem 3.1: privileged local systems (with respect to the conjugacy classes [R_i], or the pair ([R_i], delta) with delta a torsion character) satisfy the p-curvature conjecture, for any d >= 1, including the projective case (empty boundary). Section 8: an irreducible subquotient of a Z-defined variation satisfies it under extra conditions (Theorem 8.2), applied to Gauss-Manin systems of smooth projective families (Corollary 8.3).
events.delivers: Restricted class: privileged local systems on smooth quasi-projective complex varieties of any dimension with quasi-unipotent boundary monodromy. The paper says that 'it is an open question if arbitrary subquotients of a Gauss-Manin connection satisfy the p-curvature conjecture' and that a classification of privileged local systems in higher dimensions is lacking.
events.remains: General flat connections; arbitrary subquotients of Gauss-Manin connections (stated as open in Section 1); local systems outside the privileged class.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for a new restricted class in higher dimension; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Przemysław Grabowski, 'On Algebraic Integrability of Vector Fields with Rational Function Coefficients that Separate Variables', arXiv:2609.00974 (submitted 1 Sep 2026; single version). For D = sum f_i(x_i) d/dx_i over Qbar(x_1,...,x_n) (n >= 2, nonzero rational f_i), gives equivalent conditions: (1) D is p-closed modulo almost all primes; (2) an explicit condition on the partial-fraction decomposition of 1/f_i (logarithmic parts vanish, or the P_i and H_i vanish and residue spans are one-dimensional over Q with one-dimensional sum); (3) D defines an algebraically integrable foliation. Verifies a generalized Grothendieck-Katz conjecture (called the Algebraic Integrability Conjecture, Conjecture 2.2) for foliations defined by these vector fields, and gives explicit first integrals.
events.delivers: Verifies a generalized foliation/algebraic-integrability form of the conjecture for a class of separable vector fields in n >= 2 variables over Qbar. It is not the linear-ODE statement, and it does not state a counterexample. The author's acknowledgements say he was unsure whether the n = 2 equivalence 'was known' and that 'the paper [25] was identified', which the author then cites as F. Ruyong, G. Zewang and X. Siting, 'Rational first integrals of separable differential equations', Math. Comput. Sci. 19(1) (2025), art. 2; that paper was not opened.
events.remains: The linear-ODE statement in full; vector fields outside the separable class; all foliations.
events.doubts: Scope: the verified statement is a foliation-level generalization, and the author himself flags that the n = 2 equivalence may be known from [25] (Ruyong, Zewang, Siting 2025). Whether that prior paper already contains the n = 2 result was not checked.
events.direction: Verifies the (generalized) conjecture for the listed class; direction consistent with the conjecture. No counterexample.
events.object: No counterexample. The paper gives explicit coefficients and first integrals for all such algebraically integrable separable vector fields.

events.what_happened: Zihong Chen, 'p-curvature in non-commutative Hodge theory and the Kontsevich-Soibelman operad', arXiv:2609.26765 (submitted 22 Sep 2026). Concerns the Getzler-Gauss-Manin 't-connection' on the periodic cyclic homology of smooth proper Z/2-graded categories; proves a regular singularity and quasi-unipotent monodromy, affirming a conjecture of Katzarkov-Kontsevich-Pantev; uses reduction mod p and a regularity criterion due to Katz. The abstract never names the Grothendieck-Katz conjecture. Listed as a related open problem by an aggregator (emergentmind), which was read.
events.delivers: Nothing on the Grothendieck-Katz conjecture as stated. The p-curvature in the title is that of a categorical connection, a different object from the flat connections the bullet concerns.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Not about the problem as stated; discarded (different connection, different conjecture).

events.what_happened: A personal page on a traefik.me host titled '260,876 operators, 826 vanishing, 2 unexplained - and the mistake in the middle' (https://144-31-195-17.traefik.me/gk/), with linked scripts pcurv.py and sweep.py, as surfaced by search. Search excerpts say it reports a pure-Python sweep of 260,876 operators, 826 with p-curvature vanishing at every prime tried, and 2 unexplained after four filters, and that the author does not think they are counterexamples. The page could NOT be opened: fetch fails on a TLS certificate mismatch (host presents a certificate for touchspace.help). Date, author and any review are unknown.
events.delivers: Unverified: a computational counterexample search that, per the excerpts, found no counterexample and claims none.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.directly_checkable: The page links pcurv.py and sweep.py; a check would rerun them and examine the two unexplained operators. Not run; the page was not reachable.
events.doubts: Unverified: not peer-reviewed, not opened, numbers not corroborated elsewhere. The search excerpt says the 826 vanishing cases are expected to be mostly connections with algebraic solutions, so the sweep alone is not evidence of a counterexample.
events.direction: Per excerpts: no counterexample found or claimed; two unexplained cases the author regards as not counterexamples.
events.object: Per excerpts only: 826 operators with p-curvature vanishing at all tested primes, of which 2 remained unexplained after four filters. Not read directly.

disputes.summary: Grabowski's n = 2 equivalence may already be in Ruyong, Zewang and Siting (2025), 'Rational first integrals of separable differential equations', Math. Comput. Sci. 19(1), art. 2. The author says the paper was 'identified' as the source after he asked for help, and does not say whether it contains the same result. The Ruyong et al. paper was not opened (Springer redirected to an identity-provider login).

Lam and Litt state that the classical Grothendieck-Katz conjecture for Gauss-Manin connections is 'an immediate consequence' of their non-abelian Theorem 1.1.1; that case is Katz's 1972 theorem. Their Theorem A uses the hypothesis 'infinitely many p', whereas the conjecture uses 'almost all p'; the difference is recorded so the later pass can see which statement each result proves.
The year of Honda's order-one theorem is given as 1974 in Pannier's talk abstracts and cited as [Hon81] in arXiv 2510.00892. The venue and year were not verified from Honda's own text.

summary: The conjecture, as Wikipedia states it, asks for an equivalence between finite monodromy (a finite etale cover trivialising a flat connection over C) and vanishing mod-p p-curvature for almost all primes. The current Wikipedia article's lead says it 'remains unsolved, despite recent progress'. Searches (32 web searches, across the name, the conjecture's wording, the author names, and AI terms) and the arXiv full-text or HTML of most in-window preprints found no proof or disproof since 26 January 2024. The in-window events are partial. Lam and Litt (arXiv 2501.13175, January 2025) prove their own stronger linear and nonlinear conjecture for listed families, and state that proving it for certain isomonodromy equations would settle the classical conjecture. Their Theorem A (arXiv 2601.07933, January 2026) is a non-abelian Katz theorem for rank r isomonodromy foliations under 'infinitely many p', which they say yields the Gauss-Manin case (Katz 1972, already known) and new cases of the ESBT/Bost conjecture; the classical conjecture for arbitrary flat bundles is not addressed. Esnault and Groechenig (arXiv 2606.16873, June 2026) prove the conjecture for privileged local systems in any dimension (Theorem 3.1), a genuinely new class beyond rigid curves, and state that arbitrary subquotients of Gauss-Manin connections remain open. Fürnsinn and Pannier (arXiv 2510.00892, October 2025, revised March 2026) give an effective version for order-one equations, which were already settled by Honda. Xu (arXiv 2507.22056, July 2025) proves equivalence with ESBT Conjecture F, which neither settles nor refutes. Grabowski (arXiv 2609.00974, September 2026) verifies a generalized algebraic-integrability form for separable rational vector fields in n >= 2 variables; he flags that the n = 2 case may be known from a 2025 paper (Ruyong et al.), not opened here. Movasati's 2403.11829 (March 2024) was withdrawn in February 2025 and its content now sits in arXiv 2502.19988, whose Section 1 says the conjecture 'might be false' on the basis of a Lame example with no claimed counterexample. Close calls: (a) whether Esnault-Groechenig's privileged class counts as a restricted case of the bullet or a new settlement of a substantial part; (b) whether Lam-Litt's 'infinitely many p' Theorem A (a weaker hypothesis than the bullet's almost all) counts as a case of the conjecture for the bundles it covers; (c) whether Grabowski's foliation statement is the same conjecture or a generalization; (d) how much weight the withdrawn and doubted Movasati claims deserve. AI involvement: no system is credited with any mathematics in any source read. Grabowski discloses that 'No part of this paper was written by any AI' and that unnamed 'free AI models' were used for 'computing explicit examples such as explicit formulas for tan(aF)' (Example 6.7); nothing is named, so no system entry is made. Other items name no AI. An unverified page (traefik.me, 260,876-operator sweep) is reported by a search tool as an AI-written computation; it could not be opened (TLS certificate mismatch), so the AI attribution is unverified and no system is recorded. Search results about AI and open problems (OpenAI and Erdos problems, a signed BAR conjecture paper with an AI disclosure, a Yau-Tian-Donaldson paper, an Anthropic-linked Jacobian conjecture item) concern other problems and were not opened.
competing_reading: The strongest case for something settled: Esnault and Groechenig's Theorem 3.1 proves the conjecture for a class of flat connections in every dimension (privileged local systems, including projective smooth X with no boundary), where previously only rigid curves and special cases were known; a reader counting restricted resolutions could count this as an event on par with Shankar or Patel-Shankar-Whang. The strongest case against counting the in-window items as progress on the classical statement: each one either proves a stronger or non-abelian variant, reproves Katz's 1972 case, or studies an equivalent or generalized foliation statement, and the classical conjecture for general flat connections is untouched. Lam-Litt's Theorem A is also a weaker hypothesis than the classical conjecture's 'almost all p' only in the 'infinitely many p' sense, so a reader could count it as a stronger statement for the bundles it covers.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of Esnault-Groechenig 2606.16873 Theorem 3.1 and Section 8, to confirm the exact class and whether it contains bundles not already covered by Katz. (2) Lam-Litt 2601.07933 Theorem B and Section 'Finiteness of non-abelian monodromy' to see whether any classical flat bundle outside Gauss-Manin is covered. (3) The Ruyong, Zewang and Siting 2025 paper (DOI 10.1007/s11786-025-00600-w) to check whether the n = 2 case of Grabowski's theorem is already known. (4) The body of Movasati 2403.11829 (PDF not readable here) and the Lame section of 2502.19988, to see whether the author's doubt is a specific error or a conjecture about consequences. (5) The Traefik sweep page (not reachable here), to check its numbers and the two unexplained operators. (6) Katz's 1972 text (scanned PDF not readable here) for the exact Gauss-Manin statement and its hypothesis. (7) Any refereed publication or expert review of the 2025-2026 preprints, none of which were found.
